sec-head.p: A single-modality model sees only text, only images, or only audio — it misses the rich context that comes from combining multiple data types. Multimodal AI processes text, images, audio, and video together, enabling systems to understand a scene, read a chart, or listen to a voice while seeing the speaker's expression, all without retraining for every new data format.

faq-item.faq-a: Multimodal AI refers to systems that process and combine multiple data types — such as text, images, audio, and video — in a single model or pipeline. This allows the AI to understand context across modalities, like reading a chart and its caption simultaneously.

faq-item.faq-q: How is multimodal AI different from unimodal AI?
faq-item.faq-a: Unimodal AI works with only one data type, such as a text-only LLM or an image classifier. Multimodal AI fuses multiple modalities, enabling richer understanding — for example, answering questions about a video by analyzing both the audio track and visual frames.

faq-item.faq-q: What are common architectures for multimodal AI?
faq-item.faq-a: Common architectures include early fusion (combining raw inputs before encoding), late fusion (processing each modality independently and merging at the decision layer), and hybrid approaches using cross-attention. Models like CLIP, Flamingo, and GPT-4V are examples of multimodal architectures.

faq-item.faq-q: How much does multimodal AI development cost?
faq-item.faq-a: A proof-of-concept starts at $2,000 to $5,000. A full production multimodal system ranges from $10,000 to $40,000 depending on the number of modalities, data volume, and fusion complexity. Contact for a fixed-price estimate specific to your use case.

faq-item.faq-q: How long does it take to build a multimodal AI system?
faq-item.faq-a: A proof-of-concept typically takes 3 to 5 weeks. A full production system with custom fusion, evaluation, and deployment typically takes 6 to 12 weeks depending on data preprocessing needs and integration scope.
